title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
subtitle: Milanese braised veal shin
excerpt: Veal shin cross-cuts braised in white wine and stock until the meat is falling off the bone and the marrow is soft. Finished with gremolata and served with saffron risotto, this is the classic Milanese pairing.

recipe.sourceNotes: Osso buco alla milanese is the canonical dish of Milan, its name meaning 'bone with a hole'. The classic pairing with risotto alla milanese and gremolata is well-documented in Milanese and Italian cookery books from the nineteenth century onward.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, heavy pot that fits all the veal pieces in a single layer.

content.text: Osso buco is thick cross-cuts of veal shin braised in white wine and stock until the meat pulls away from the bone and the marrow in the centre turns soft and rich. Gremolata, a mixture of lemon zest, garlic, and parsley, is scattered over at the end to cut through the richness of the braise. The traditional accompaniment is saffron risotto.

items.preparation: each about 4 cm thick and 300 g

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Tie kitchen twine around the circumference of each veal piece to help it hold its shape during cooking. Season the flour with salt and pepper and coat each piece all over.
Heat the oil in a large dutch oven over a medium-high heat. Brown the veal pieces well on both sides, about 4 minutes per side. Lift out and set aside.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook over a medium heat for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes, scraping the base. Add the tomatoes and stock. Nestle the veal pieces into the pot upright so the marrow does not fall out. Tuck in the bay and thyme.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook in the oven for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours, until the meat is very tender and pulling away from the bone.
Mix the lemon zest, grated garlic, and parsley together for the gremolata. Remove the twine and bay leaves from the veal. Scatter the gremolata over and serve.
